**Weekend Woodworking Project – Simple Pine Side‑Table** A compact, useful piece that can be cut, assembled and finished in one weekend. All steps and tool recommendations come from the beginner‑side‑table guide in the knowledge base [[summaries/session-03_2023-11-13]] and the supporting concepts [[concepts/basic-tools]] & [[concepts/woodworking-safety]]. --- ## 1. Project Overview | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Piece** | Small side table (≈ 16 in × 16 in top, 20 in high) | | **Wood** | Soft pine (affordable, easy to work) – [[entities/pine]] | | **Cut list** | • Top: 2 × 1×8 boards, 16 in each (glued edge‑to‑edge)
• Legs: 4 × 1×2 boards, 20 in each
• Aprons: 2 × 1×3 @ 13 in (long sides)
• Aprons: 2 × 1×3 @ 11 in (short sides) | | **Fasteners** | 1¼ in wood screws for aprons‑to‑legs; 1 in screws for tabletop attachment | --- ## 2. Basic Tools & Materials (as listed in the guide) | Tool / Material | Why it’s needed | |-----------------|-----------------| | Tape measure – [[entities/tape-measure]] | Accurate layout and cuts | | Pencil – [[entities/pencil]] | Marking cut lines and screw locations | | Carpenter’s square – [[entities/carpenter-square]] | Ensuring 90° corners | | Handsaw – [[entities/handsaw]] | Cutting pine boards | | Drill‑driver – [[entities/drill-driver]] (with drill‑bits & screwdriver bits) | Drilling pilot holes & driving screws | | Quick‑grip clamps – [[entities/quick-grip-clamp]] (2 medium) | Holding joints while glue sets | | Sandpaper – [[entities/sandpaper]] | Smoothing surfaces before finishing | | Safety gear (safety glasses, hearing protection) – per [[concepts/woodworking-safety]] | Protect eyes & ears | | Wood glue (PVA) | Adds strength to tabletop edge joint | | Finish (oil, wax or paint) – optional | Protects wood & adds appearance | --- ## 3. Weekend Timeline & Step‑by‑Step Plan ### **Saturday – Prep & Rough‑Cut** | Time | Activity | |------|----------| | 08:00‑09:00 | **Safety set‑up** – put on glasses, ear protection; clear work area. | | 09:00‑10:00 | **Lay out & mark** – use tape measure, pencil and square to mark all cuts on the pine boards (follow the cut list). | | 10:00‑12:00 | **Rough cuts** – cut top boards, legs, and aprons with the handsaw. | | 12:00‑13:00 | **Lunch break** | | 13:00‑14:00 | **Fine‑tune cuts** – check lengths, sand any high spots. | | 14:00‑15:00 | **Glue tabletop** – apply wood glue to the long edges of the two top boards, clamp together (quick‑grip clamps), wipe excess. | | 15:00‑16:00 | **Dry time** – let glue cure (≈ 30 min); meanwhile, **sand** the cut edges of legs and aprons. | | 16:00‑17:00 | **Prep for assembly** – drill pilot holes in all aprons (slightly larger than screw shank to allow wood movement, as recommended). | ### **Sunday – Assembly & Finish** | Time | Activity | |------|----------| | 08:00‑09:00 | **Assemble two “L” corners** – attach one leg to a long apron with 1¼ in screws; use the square to verify right angles; clamp. | | 09:00‑10:00 | **Join the two corners** – connect with the remaining aprons (both long and short) using the same screw pattern; check overall squareness. | | 10:00‑11:00 | **Attach tabletop** – flip base upside‑down, position glued tabletop, drill pilot holes through aprons, drive 1 in screws from underneath. | | 11:00‑12:00 | **Final sanding** – run sandpaper over all surfaces, especially edges and screw heads. | | 12:00‑13:00 | **Lunch break** | | 13:00‑15:00 | **Finishing** – apply chosen finish (oil, wax, or paint); let dry according to product instructions. | | 15:00‑16:00 | **Clean‑up & review** – remove clamps, wipe workbench, admire the completed table! | --- ## 4. Key Safety & Quality Tips (from [[concepts/woodworking-safety]]) 1. **Clamp before cutting or drilling** – prevents movement and splintering. 2. **Keep hands clear of cutting paths** – let the tool do the work. 3. **Wear eye protection at all times**. 4. **Allow tools to stop completely before setting them down**. 5. **Use pilot holes sized slightly larger than the screw shank** – gives “play” for seasonal wood movement and avoids splitting (as the guide notes). --- ## 5. Quick‑Check Checklist - [ ] All pine pieces cut to exact dimensions - [ ] Pilot holes drilled in aprons & tabletop - [ ] Squares confirm 90° corners at every joint - [ ] Clamps securely hold glue joints for at least 30 min - [ ] All screws driven just snug – no overtightening (prevents wood stress) - [ ] Surface sanded smooth; finish applied evenly --- **Result:** By following this plan you’ll finish a solid, functional side table in one weekend, using only the basic hand‑ and power‑tools highlighted in your knowledge base. Enjoy the satisfaction of creating another piece of furniture for your home!
